stem: Why should the number of joints not automatically be used as the mobility of a closed-loop mechanism?

options.text: Loop-closure constraints can make joint coordinates dependent; the slide points to a mobility criterion such as Grübler’s.
Closed loops always have zero mobility regardless of geometry.
Its mobility is always the sum of individual joint freedoms, without subtracting independent loop-closure constraints.
Its mobility is always exactly the number of actuators, even when passive joints or dependent drives are present.

stem: A mechanism has fewer independent freedoms than a general task requires. Is calling this mismatch “redundancy” justified?

options.text: No, because redundancy refers only to duplicated controllers and never to robot motion.
No. Redundancy means excess task-relative freedom; too few freedoms can make the general task infeasible.
Yes. Any mismatch between mechanism DOF and task DOF is redundancy.
Yes, provided the mechanism is serial rather than closed-loop.

stem: For the fixed-frame planar 2R map x=l₁cosθ₁+l₂cos(θ₁+θ₂), y=l₁sinθ₁+l₂sin(θ₁+θ₂), define s₁=sinθ₁, c₁=cosθ₁, s₁₂=sin(θ₁+θ₂), c₁₂=cos(θ₁+θ₂). With positive link lengths and θ₂∈[−π,π], which complete Jacobian, determinant and singularity statement is correct? Rows correspond to (x,y), columns to (θ₁,θ₂).

options.text: J=[[-l₁s₁−l₂s₁₂, +l₂s₁₂], [l₁c₁+l₂c₁₂, −l₂c₁₂]]; det J=−l₁l₂sinθ₂; singular at θ₂=0,±π.

J=[[-l₁s₁, −l₂s₁₂], [l₁c₁, l₂c₁₂]]; det J=l₁l₂sinθ₂; singular at θ₂=0,±π.

assumptions: Ideal planar 2R chain, positive link lengths, fixed base, and a two-coordinate position task rather than full spatial pose.
